# The answers this build produced, retained so a later build can be compared with it.
# GENERATED by eng/run-differential.py --write. A `#diverges` line is authored: it
# names a case that is EXPECTED to differ from the comparison engine, and the reason.
#diverges broiler-js 1 Broiler.JS's `console.log` writes nothing and returns its argument, so a program that reports through `console` has no output. The Console Standard's `log` prints its arguments through the Logger and returns `undefined`
#diverges broiler-js 2 Broiler.JS throws listing the `console` object's own names; `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` of an ordinary object, which the `console` namespace is, never throws
#diverges broiler-js 3 Broiler.JS's message for that error names a platform type; the language leaves message text to the implementation, and a type from the engine's own build is nothing a program can use
#diverges broiler-js 4 Broiler.JS's error `stack` names source files of the engine's own build and hands them to guest code; the language defines no `stack`, and this realm gives an error none
#diverges broiler-js 5 Broiler.JS lists one of `String.prototype`'s own names twice; `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` of an ordinary object lists each key once
#diverges broiler-js 6 Broiler.JS's `for … in` finds no key through a `Proxy` on the prototype chain and calls none of its traps; enumeration reads each object on the chain through its own `[[OwnPropertyKeys]]` and `[[GetOwnProperty]]`
#diverges broiler-js 7 Broiler.JS's global object has an own property named `import`, which is host-defined: the language defines no global by that name, and a program cannot reference it as a binding
#diverges broiler-js 8 Broiler.JS's poisoned global store: after a `with` head threw, an indirect `eval` restores the global `var` binding to its value at that moment, 1 where the program assigned 2. The language gives a `with` statement no such effect
#diverges broiler-js 9 the same, a second time: the assignment of 3 is undone as well, because the snapshot is permanent rather than restored once
